t: You're looking at Cambridge Terrace, a row of consecutive terraced mansions overlooking Regent's Park. The terrace has been Grade I listed since 1974. It was designed by John Nash, the Georgian and Regency architect who shaped many important areas of London in the neoclassical and picturesque styles. His designs were financed by the Prince Regent and by the property developer James Burton, and he often collaborated with Burton's son, Decimus Burton.
